pr_title: Cast to at least 32 bit unsigned type when shifting left 24 places
pr_body:
Fixes #11853

Implicit C promotion rules apply so the value is promoted to int otherwise and that might not be big enough when the value is then left-shifted 24 places.
pr_comments: As a matter of experimenting, would `*p++ << 24U` work as well?
Why not be consistent?

> Why not be consistent?

ok, but it's not even nice to disseminate code of (unsigned int).
The problem is not C, but the -fsanitize = undefined parameter of gcc.
If I compile with gcc only i have no error

> As a matter of experimenting, would `*p++ << 24U` work as well?

I do not know, and I am not sure it makes sense to even try, because that is much more ugly.

> > Why not be consistent?
> 
> ok, but it's not even nice to disseminate code of (unsigned int).
> The problem is not C, but the -fsanitize = undefined parameter of gcc.
> If I compile with gcc only i have no error

That does not mean that the undefined behavior of overflowing the value into the sign is not triggered. Of course in reality it will work because the shift into the sign will produce exactly the same value when finally cast to unsigned int.

> ok, but it's not even nice to disseminate code of (unsigned int).

And to this - feel free to submit a later PR that replaces all the usage of unsigned int in that source file with something else. But that is clearly for a different PR than this one that fixes a concrete build breakage.

> Of course in reality it will work because the shift into the sign will produce exactly the same value when finally cast to unsigned int.

Being undefined, it does not need to be the same value. It might
preserve the sign, or not, depending on the platform.

On the other hand, a right shift on a signed type is implementation
defined, and we should avoid that too.

> And to this - feel free to submit a later PR 

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/11860

> > As a matter of experimenting, would `*p++ << 24U` work as well?
> 
> I do not know, and I am not sure it makes sense to even try, because that is much more ugly.

It would not work, FWIW.
I would prefer to fix here only what is necessary to make the test case work.

issue_context.title: Master build is K.O. :  runtime error: left shift of 184 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
issue_context.body:
See  https://travis-ci.org/github/openssl/openssl/builds/687826428

Config: 
```
EXTENDED_TEST="yes" CONFIG_OPTS="no-asm enable-ubsan enable-rc5 enable-md2 enable-ssl3 enable-ssl3-method enable-nextprotoneg no-shared enable-buildtest-c++ -fno-sanitize=alignment -DFUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION -Wno-unused-command-line-argument" CXX="clang++" 
```

Ouput :
```
read DSA key
crypto/pem/pvkfmt.c:42:18: runtime error: left shift of 184 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
../../util/wrap.pl ../../apps/openssl dsa -pubin -pubout -in msb-f.d -inform d -out msb-ff.dd -outform d => 1
    not ok 5 - d -> d

crypto/pem/pvkfmt.c:42:18: runtime error: left shift of 184 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
../../util/wrap.pl ../../apps/openssl dsa -pubin -pubout -in msb-f.d -inform d -out msb-ff.dp -outform p => 1
...
    not ok 8 - d -> p
    #   Failed test 'd -> p'
    #   at ../../test/recipes/tconversion.pl line 70.
```
comments:
Hmmm...  here's the code section where that happens:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/4fcd15c18ad6b5523a389863d3e5628d44db6eb4/crypto/pem/pvkfmt.c#L35-L45

Not a signed int in sight as far as I can see...  if you know how to fix it, PR welcome!

I think always casting `(unsigned int)*p++` should fix it. Well, it should be sufficient in the last case, but just for uniformity. Because the *p++ is promoted to int and then you try to shift it too much. The automatic conversion to unsigned int comes only after that.
I would love to read the reasoning behind coercing the dereference of a pointer to an unsigned value to something signed. That makes zero sense to me...

That's C :grin: No need to seek reasoning. If you automatically convert something smaller (even if unsigned) to int and the "something smaller" fits, it is promoted to int and not unsigned int. And 184 fits into int.
Let's just say that C seems to become weirder as time goes :confused:

> That's C  No need to seek reasoning. If you automatically convert something smaller (even if unsigned) to int and the "something smaller" fits, it is promoted to int and not unsigned int. And 184 fits into int.

To give chapter and verse, for C99 (well, n1256.pdf, the last free draft version), see section 6.3.1.1 clause 2
I wonder why both competing PRs seem to fix other places where no runtime error happens?
We should have probably flagged #11857 as `urgent`, as many PRs are failing on this!
If it was "really" urgent the author should have split the urgent part out in a separate PR.
